transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-07
Time: 10:00 AM PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Recording: (auto)
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Samir Gupta (Redwood SE), Maya Torres (Head of ML, Halcyon), Ethan Cole (CTO), Priya Singh (Eng Mgr)

Summary:
Quick discovery to understand Halcyon Analytics' current embedding/rerank architecture, integration constraints with their vector DB, expected throughput and latency targets, and whether Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment fits their security and cost constraints. Customer interested in hybrid search (BM25 + ANN) and LLM-based reranking.

Topics:
- Current stack and pain points (search relevance, slow rerank latency)
- Vector DB options and integration (Pinecone, Milvus, Qdrant, self-hosted)
- Throughput and dimensionality (512 vs 1536 vs 2048 dims)
- Hybrid search and rerank architecture (retrieve-then-rerank)
- Deployment modes: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/KMS/SOC2)
- Pilot and benchmarking plan

Action items (captured in metadata): Lena to send pricing/pilot terms; Samir to share benchmark plan; Maya to provide sample dataset.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining on a Tuesday morning. quick round of intros  
 - I'm Lena, AE on the enterprise team, Samir is our SE who will dig into perf details.
[00:15] Maya (Halcyon): Hey, Maya here, Head of ML at Halcyon. We run search and QA features over our knowledge base. Ethan's on for infra questions, Priya will be our eng lead.
[00:30] Ethan (Halcyon): Hi all.
[00:35] Samir (Redwood): Quick agenda, we'll talk current infra, embedding dims, vector DB, retrieval+rerank flow, and then figure out a pilot. Sound good?
[00:42] Maya: Yep, sounds good. we're mostly focused on relevance, current system is slower after we added cross-encoder rerank, latency spikes.
[00:55] Priya: yeah, we see tail latency when we run rerank on large result sets, especially during peak traffic. throughput becomes a problem.
[01:10] Lena: Can you walk through the current stack, what vector DB and embedding models you're using?
[01:20] Maya: Sure - we currently embed with an in-house model, dim is 1024, stored in Milvus self-hosted cluster. For retrieval we use HNSW ANN, top-k 1,000, then feed to a cross-encoder transformer for rerank. That reranker is our main cost and latency thing.
[01:40] Samir: Got it. So retrieve big candidate set then cross-encode. What's your QPS and acceptable latency for end users?
[01:50] Priya: At peak we do ~200 qps, average 60 qps. Our SLA target is p95 < 500ms for search end-to-end but with rerank right now we're around 1.2s p95.
[02:05] Ethan: Also want to mention we have strict data residency and PII - some documents require encryption at rest with KMS and audit logs.
[02:18] Lena: Thanks. On the model side, have you considered moving to a smaller embed dim or switching to a provider model? Any cost concerns?
[02:28] Maya: We're worried about quality loss if we drop dims - for some of our longer docs we need the richer representation. But cost is a factor; serving millions of vectors at 1536 dim is expensive.
[02:42] Samir: Two things we've seen - one: you can quantize vectors for storage to reduce footprint; two: using Redwood's prefix cache and batching for hosted/dedicated reduces per-request tokens/compute. For embeddings we support 768, 1024, 1536, and customer models.
[03:05] Maya: How does integration with Milvus or Pinecone look? We prefer not to rip-and-replace Milvus right away.
[03:12] Samir: Redwood supports both approaches: you can host embeddings on Redwood and use our vector store integrations (Pinecone connector, Qdrant/Milvus via S3/FS export) or you can keep Milvus and call Redwood's reranker/LLM as a service. For Hosted, we often run the embed+rerank in our cloud and write vectors to your DB; for Dedicated you get reserved capacity endpoints closer to your network for lower latency.
[03:38] Maya: Any pitfalls in hybrid search - combining BM25 and ANN?
[03:44] Samir: Hybrid typically runs BM25 to get lexical signals, concat with ANN top-k then rerank. You need to tune weights and normalization - something our Optimize team helps with. Also chunking matters: if you're chunking long docs at 500 tokens vs 200 it changes recall.
[04:02] Priya: We're chunking at 512 tokens with 50% overlap. That gave good recall but increased vector count a lot.
[04:12] Lena: On throughput, for 200 qps with top-k 100 retrieval and a cross-encoder rerank of 100 we recommend Dedicated or Hosted with dedicated GPUs - otherwise cost for inference on large cross-encoders becomes prohibitive.
[04:30] Ethan: What's the difference in cost and control between Hosted and Dedicated? We need predictable bills for forecasting.
[04:38] Samir: Hosted is pay-as-you-go on our public cloud, good for short experiments; Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with monthly commitment and predictable unit economics. Private gives VPC/on-prem for strict compliance. For your 200 qps and cross-encoder rerank, Dedicated with reserved capacity or a hybrid where retrieval stays in your cluster and rerank hits Redwood Dedicated endpoints tends to be the best tradeoff.
[05:05] Maya: If we keep Milvus for storage but use Redwood for rerank, do we send raw text or ids?
[05:12] Samir: Usually flow is: client queries -> Milvus returns top-k vector ids -> you send either the corresponding doc chunks or a prebuilt context to Redwood's reranker endpoint along with an instruction to rerank. Sending the minimal text necessary reduces tokens. We also support passing embeddings directly if you want the LLM to score vector similarities without re-embedding.
[05:36] Priya: latency wise, what's realistic for the rerank call? Cross-encoder, say re-ranking 100 docs, what's p95?
[05:44] Samir: On a dedicated GPU with optimized kernels we see ~120-200ms for a cross-encoder on 100 items (depends on model size and sequence length). On hosted shared infra it can be 200-400ms. Total end-to-end includes retrieval and network hops.
[06:04] Maya: Hmm that would be close to our 500ms target if retrieval is fast. Retrieval from Milvus in our VPC is about 50-80ms.
[06:14] Ethan: One more - embedding dimensionality. We have vectors at 1024 now but we were considering moving to a 1536 model for quality. Storage increases roughly linearly; any Redwood recommendations?
[06:26] Samir: Dimension vs quality tradeoff - 1536 often helps for certain corpora but you can try distillation/quantization. Redwood's Optimize can run quant profiles and recommend per-workload dims and quantization (like int8) to reduce storage and throughput costs while preserving quality.
[06:46] Maya: Is quantization lossy for reranking quality?
[06:49] Samir: Some loss, but in many cases small. We recommend an eval set to measure delta. Our evaluation harness can run A/B tests.
[06:59] Maya: We also asked about hybrid search ranking - do you recommend retrieval-then-rerank or a single-stage approach?
[07:05] Samir: Retrieval-then-rerank remains the most cost-effective for high quality: ANN to get top-k, then a cross-encoder or lightweight re-score. Single-stage dense retrieval with larger models is possible but expensive at scale.
[07:18] Priya: On security, we need SOC2, SSO (SAML/Okta), KMS integration, and audit logs for access. Is that in Private/Dedicated?
[07:28] Lena: SOC2 is standard for Redwood Hosted; Dedicated and Private give you more control - Private includes VPC peering options, customer-managed KMS, and audit logs shipped to your SIEM. We'll share the security pack.
[07:42] Ethan: For PII, can we keep vectors on-prem and still use Redwood's reranker?
[07:48] Samir: Yes - you can keep your vectors on-prem and call Redwood's rerank endpoints over a secure peered connection, or run Redwood Private on-prem to keep everything internal. The tradeoff is operational overhead for Private.
[08:00] Maya: About benchmarks - we want realistic numbers on cost and latency for three setups: 1) Hosted end-to-end, 2) Dedicated rerank + Milvus retrieval, 3) Private on-prem.
[08:12] Samir: We'll put together a perf spreadsheet. For the pilot we'll want your sample dataset (1-3M chunks), typical query patterns, and success metrics: p95 latency, relevance delta, and cost per 1k queries.
[08:28] Priya: We can provide a 500k chunk sample first.
[08:32] Lena: Great. For the pilot, recommended steps: we run a small benchmark within Hosted to baseline; then if you're happy we scope a Dedicated pilot with reserved capacity to meet your 200 qps. If there's strict compliance, we propose Private.
[08:48] Maya: Any notes about vector indexing parameters - efConstruction, efSearch for HNSW - we want guidance for recall vs latency tuning.
[08:58] Samir: We can advise on HNSW parameters. efConstruction affects build time and index size; efSearch trades recall for latency. For 1M vectors efSearch 100-200 is typical for decent recall at latency ~20-50ms. We'll include recommended knobs in the perf doc.
[09:15] Ethan: Are there prebuilt connectors to Milvus so we don't need manual exports?
[09:20] Samir: We have documented connectors and templates; full-managed connectors are better for Hosted, while for Dedicated we can assist with a small adapter.
[09:30] Maya: Cost - how do you price rerank calls? Is it per-token / per-inference?
[09:36] Lena: Pricing for Hosted is per-token/compute and per-embedding; Dedicated is unit-based reserved capacity. For rerank we may charge per-request compute units; we'll send a pricing sheet with examples.
[09:48] Priya: What's the expected time to get a Dedicated pilot up?
[09:52] Lena: Typically 2-4 weeks to provision reserved pool and run initial tests, faster if you accept hosted pilot first.
[09:58] Maya: Ok. Any red flags for us?
[10:01] Samir: Just two things - 1) keep candidate set as small as feasible (like top-100) to control rerank cost, and 2) measure quality delta when changing vector dim or quantization. We'll help run those evals.
[10:14] Priya: Noted.
[10:16] Lena: Closing recap: Lena to send pricing and pilot terms; Samir to share benchmark plan and recommended HNSW knobs; Halcyon to share 500k sample and success metrics. We'll schedule hands-on perf week of Apr 20.
[10:32] Maya: Thanks everyone.
[10:35] Ethan: Thanks.
[10:36] Samir: Thanks - we'll follow up with docs and a spreadsheet.
[10:40] Lena: Bye.

Notes on transcript quality: Auto transcription had a few name mislabels (Milvus sometimes appears as "milvish"), and product names occasionally mangled (e.g., "Redwood Dedicated" transcribed as "Redwood Dedicate").
